_comment: Mutation survivors accepted as a baseline for the binding sweep (the membership walk, the context it carries, and the frontend). The nightly ratchet fails when a survivor appears outside this set, and when an entry is no longer a survivor. Regenerate with `python scripts/mutation_gate.py --baseline walk --update` after a sweep, and only ever let this set shrink. Entries are the survivor line without its line:col position, so they survive unrelated code motion.

_accepted.crates/valgebra-py/src/build/classes.rs:: The guard `!origin.is_instance_of::<PyType>()` keeps a class origin from asking the `typing_extensions` table, and the mutant asks it for a class and skips it for a form. On the interpreter this sweep runs, 3.12 with `typing_extensions` installed from the lock, that module's `Required` and `NotRequired` are `typing`'s own objects, from 3.11 on, and the loop above has already matched them: the table answers `false` for every origin that reaches the guard, on either side of it, and the mutant moves cost alone. So the frontend's arms for that module's own objects answer what the `typing` arms already answered, and a mutant of them moves nothing a test can read. They answer where the module defines objects of its own -- 3.10, or the stand-in `a_typing_extensions_form_reads_as_its_typing_spelling` installs on an interpreter that cannot import the module, which is where that corpus row kills this mutant. The arm dies with the 3.10 floor.
_accepted.crates/valgebra-py/src/build/generics.rs: `is_extension(any) || is_extension(never)` becomes `is_extension(any) && is_extension(never)`, and no object is both. On the interpreter this sweep runs, 3.12 with `typing_extensions` installed from the lock, that module's `Any` and `Never` are `typing`'s own objects, from 3.11 on, which `refuse_literal_form` has already compared by identity before it asks this, so both read `false` for any argument that reaches them and either spelling reads `false`. So the arms for that module's own objects answer what the `typing` arms already answered, and a mutant of them moves nothing a test can read. They answer where the module defines objects of its own -- 3.10, or the stand-in `a_typing_extensions_form_reads_as_its_typing_spelling` installs on an interpreter that cannot import the module, which is where that corpus row kills this mutant. The two arms die with the 3.10 floor.

The mask chooses between asking the interpreter for a name and not asking, and asking is what the frontend did before the mask existed: `getattr_opt` answers correctly for a name that is there and for one that is not. So a mutant of the mask can only move cost, which is `scripts/perf_gate.py --binding-annotated`'s business and not a test's. The direction that would matter -- skipping a name a marker really carries -- is not equivalent and is not excused: the corpus asks a marker of each shape a name can live in (a `slots` type, an instance dictionary, a `__getattr__` hook, and a type with both), and the mutants that skipped a carried name die on those rows. The file is `build/refine.rs` since the frontend's surfaces moved beside the dispatch; this baseline is keyed by path, so a mutant whose file moves reads as a new one until its key does too.

_accepted.crates/valgebra-py/src/check/index.rs: d: `if !fields.is_empty()` read as `if fields.is_empty()`: an attribute record with no fields gains a plan of no names, and one with fields gains none. Both halves are cost. A plan of no names is what a record of no fields would get anyway, and a record with fields falls back to its own text. The walk falls back for a schema the index does not carry -- every plan lookup in `check/walk/` is `Option`-shaped with the fallback written beside it -- so a traversal that skips a node decides the same values and only pays more for them.
_accepted.crates/valgebra-py/src/check/index.rs: r: The traversal `__traverse__` hands the cycle collector. Every object it yields is an interned `str`, and a `str` refers to nothing, so it can be no edge of a cycle and a collector that never sees one still collects correctly. The method exists because a traversal omitting an owned reference is wrong on its own terms, not because this omission leaks: no test can distinguish the two, and none should be written to.
_accepted.crates/valgebra-py/src/check/memo.rs: re: `<=` differs from `<` only at a reference naming index 128, the first past the plan's `u128`. `plan` names nothing for a table longer than `PLANNED_DEFINITIONS`, and a validator's references name its own definitions, so no reference the plan reads names that index. The comparison keeps an index outside the table from shifting a `u128` past its width, a panic in a debug build and a wrapped bit in a release one, for a schema no validator holds.

The arming, `bits | USED | ARMED`, read as `bits | USED ^ ARMED`: `^` binds tighter than `|`, so the mutant is `bits | (USED ^ ARMED)`, and on two distinct bits `^` is `|`. The word set is the same word.

The restore, `bits & !ARMED | outer`: `outer` is the armed flag the member was walked inside, or nothing, and the mask has just cleared that flag, so `^` sets it where `|` does and leaves it clear where `|` does. The word after the member is the same word.

`calling`, the definitions whose own bodies call code, folds one bit per definition, `1 << at` at the definition's own index, and the enumeration reaches each index once: no bit is folded in twice, and on bits folded in once `^` sets what `|` sets. The set is the same, and so is every bit of the plan read from it.

`remembered`, the definitions reaching no code the walk calls, folds one bit per definition, `1 << at` at the definition's own index, and the enumeration reaches each index once: no bit is folded in twice, and on bits folded in once `^` sets what `|` sets. The set is the same, and so is every bit of the plan read from it.
_accepted.crates/valgebra-py/src/check/walk/record: Cannot change an answer. A mapping of a `str` key and an `int` value falls to the arm every other pair of scalar kinds takes, which asks the same two tests through `scalar_admits` and reads the dict through the same scan; only the dispatch on each half's kind at every entry is added. That is cost, and the instruction gate counts it: `scripts/perf_gate.py --binding-mapping`, a `dict[str, int]`, reads 17.5% more without the arm, past its 2% ceiling.

`plan.by_name.len() == fields.len()` holds of every plan, which lists each field once, so `||` takes the plan for every record: a record whose clause reads keys and declares no more than `SMALL_OBJECT` fields among them. The plan and the search answer alike for such a record -- each reads the document's last value for every field and asks the clause of the keys left -- so only the cost moves, and the instruction gate's `--binding-json-open` reads it: that shape's record declares one field. `a_record_reading_keys_takes_its_plan_past_a_small_object` holds the crossing itself.

Cannot change a report. The counter it disables is what lets a closed record holding exactly its own keys skip a scan that would find nothing: stuck at zero, the count matches only an empty value, so every other record falls through to the scan and the scan reports what the count would have. Only the cost moves, and cost is the instruction budget's business. The other half of the same condition is not equivalent and is killed by tests/test_mutation.py: a value that grows while it is explained leaves the count matching entries it no longer has, which is why the length is read again before the skip is taken.
_accepted.crates/valgebra-py/src/check/walk/scalar: The mutant's body is the function's own: the error is a parameter, and a parameter is dropped where its function returns, so `()` drops it at the very place `drop(err)` does -- inside `set_aside`, out of line, which is the whole of what the function is for. Inlined into `check_refine`'s loop over its constraints, the drop's read of whether the thread is attached has its thread-local address taken ahead of the loop, once for every refined value; out of line, it is taken only where the error a string holding a lone surrogate raises is dropped. The original and the mutant compile to the same function, so neither a test nor a count can tell them apart.

The ends of the band, and the 3.14 and free-threaded readings, are held by the measurements in the function's doc comment and by no count, which `docs/dev/07-tooling-ci.md` records.
